title: Messier 77 (MIRI + NIRCam)
caption: The barred spiral galaxy Messier 77, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: constellation Cetus · about 45 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Webb Picture of the Month (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A glowing bar crosses the center of this spiral galaxy, ringed by glittering stars and dust. From each side of the ring a spiral arm winds outward, and faint dark red dust clouds swirl through the disc. Six long rays and two short ones radiate from the core. This is Messier 77, a barred spiral 45 million light-years away in Cetus, the Whale.

The rays are diffraction spikes, made by Webb's optics, not the galaxy. They appear because the core is extremely bright and compact. It is an active galactic nucleus, powered by a supermassive black hole eight million times the mass of the Sun, where gas crashes together in tight orbit and releases enormous radiation.

The ring, more than 6 000 light-years across, is a starburst ring, packed with intense star formation seen as dense orange bubbles. Webb's view also reveals the central bar, which does not appear in visible-light images.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.10 x 2.13 arcminutes) and distance (45 million light years), the frame spans roughly 27,000 × 28,000 light-years. Its light set out about 45 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines Webb's NIRCam and MIRI. Light at 1.5 micrometers is blue, 1.87 micrometers (hydrogen) cyan, 3.0 micrometers (water ice) green, and 3.35, 7.7 and 21 micrometers red.
understand.eye: All of this light is infrared and invisible to the eye, and the spikes come from the telescope's optics rather than the galaxy.

explore: Webb's Mid-Infrared Instrument adds the glow of interstellar dust in dark red, forming a huge vortex of swirling filaments with cavities between them. Along the southern arm, NIRCam also traces light from complex molecules called polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.
alt: An infrared spiral galaxy with a glowing central bar, a glittering ring of stars and dust, two winding arms, faint dark red dust, and six long and two short rays from the center.
